title: ASF Dev Agent — implementation plan
description: The implementation map a Dev Lead signs before work starts: what gets touched, in which order, what is already there, what is deliberately left out, and what still needs deciding. This file in docs/.asf/schema/ is the single source: KStudio validates against it and the coding CLI writes against it. Version 2 drops the bookkeeping that version 1 required — the log of files read, and the file list repeated inside impacts — and no longer requires a test command to be stated, because a repo's test commands belong to the repo (its CLAUDE.md and .gitlab-ci.yml), not to a plan. A plan is read by a person: produce the map, not an inventory of your own work.

schema.description: Write `asf.dev-plan/2`. Version 1 is still accepted when reading: plans written before 2026-10-04 are stored in sessions, and a reader that rejected them would make a signed plan unreadable by the thing that validated it.

summary.description: What the epic asks for and what already exists, in prose. Name the contradictions you found between documents here: that is what the signer cannot get anywhere else.

existing.description: What already exists and must not be redone, by name — a module, an endpoint, a table.

read.description: Optional and not expected: the paths you read. Tracking this costs more than it is worth to the signer. Leave it out.

steps.description: The map. One step is one layer of one repo, and carries the files it touches: this is what the Dev Lead signs, and what makes the work reviewable before it exists.

files.description: The files this step touches. A file that does not exist yet is named as you intend to create it — no need to verify a path you are about to write.

impacts.description: The same work seen by module instead of by step: it answers «what does this epic disturb», which a list of steps does not. The files stay in the steps — do not repeat them here.

files.description: Optional and ignored: the files belong to the steps. Here they would be a second list to keep in sync with the first.

tests.description: Which levels of test this epic needs, and where. State them; do not run anything to find out — the commands live in each repo's CLAUDE.md and .gitlab-ci.yml.

command.description: Optional: only if it differs from the repo's own.

covers.description: The acceptance criteria this test level covers, as RF-NN/AC-NN.

questions.description: What you could not decide and a person must clarify. Empty is a claim, not a default: it says every contradiction you met is resolved in the summary. Questions never block signing: they are clarifications, answered at any time in the chat. A question is a string, or an object with a stable id (Q1, Q2, ...) once it has to carry its answer: when the person answers Qn, write their words in `risposta` and the date in `risposta_at`, never delete or renumber a question, and change steps/impacts/out_of_plan only if the answer changes them.

out_of_plan.description: Work this epic deliberately leaves out, named and justified. Silence here is the expensive kind.
